author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.
decisions:
Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.

The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected. The correction offers the current values, is held to the same rules as a booking, and replaces the original rather than adding a second visit. Cancelling a visit stays out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Given a booked visit, when its correction is opened, then that visit's current date and description are offered for changing.
Given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted, then that visit carries the new values and the owner's record is shown.
Given a booked visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet has no more visits than before.
Given a blank description or a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused and offered again with the offending field named.
Edge case 3: a correction naming an owner, a pet, and a visit that do not belong together is refused rather than applied.
Edge case 4: a visit whose date has already passed cannot be corrected while keeping that date, because a correction is held to the same future-date rule as a booking.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit — NG-5 keeps this out.
Deleting a visit — NG-4 is untouched by this slice.
Any link into the correction from the owner detail page. The owner decided the correction is reached only by opening it directly, and named a visible entry point as a possible follow-up request.
Changing which pet a visit belongs to — only the date and the description are correctable.
notes: Owner-specified interface constraints, quoted from the intake request (line 1) and binding on design: 'GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit` model attribute.' and 'POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required, date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place - the pet must not gain an additional visit record - and redirects to the owner detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.' | Non-goal ADR: docs/adr/2026-09-08-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing.md narrows NG-5; the 2026-08-08 ADR's status line now records the amendment. The ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md is outside my write scope - system-design-expert should add it. | Edge case 3 is my narrowest reading, not an owner statement: it extends the recorded booking rule (Visits edge case 1) to the correction surface. | Two open questions recorded in the PRD rather than blocked on: a visible entry point, and whether a past-dated visit should be correctable.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The correction is the nested-edit-under-owner shape the package already demonstrates, applied to the visit surface. PetController is the adjacent seam: findPet (PetController.java:75-87) loads an aggregate member through an optional {petId} path variable, and updatePetDetails (PetController.java:186-200) writes the change through the aggregate root. VisitController gets the same treatment with {visitId}. No new package, bean, dependency, repository, or pattern; system-design Overview (Owner is the aggregate entry point, no VisitRepository), Package Structure, and Persistence all hold unchanged. The one adjustment is a parameter: the controller-wide @ModelAttribute loadPetWithVisit gains an optional visitId and branches, exactly as findPet does. docs/system-design.md was updated for the Contracts rows and one State Machine sentence; docs/adr/README.md gained the index row for the product expert's narrowing ADR (2026-09-08-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing.md), and the 2026-08-08 row's Status cell now names the narrowing so the index matches that ADR's amended status line. No new ADR: the narrowing is already recorded, and every design choice here is contained by this slice and follows a demonstrated pattern.
integration_points: HTTP surface: GET and POST on /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, added to the existing VisitController. No new controller, no new bean, no new route prefix. Security-principles Realization row 'Widening the exposed surface': the correction is open to any caller, identical to the existing booking POST beside it, so the change is not weaker than the recorded baseline (system-design.md#security-context).

Repository boundary (OwnerRepository) in VisitControllerTests: keep the class's established @MockitoBean stub, returning a real Owner-Pet-Visit graph built in init(). Assertions run against that real aggregate, which the controller mutates in place, not against the stub. CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy tolerates the existing Mockito use here; introducing a second, different double for the same boundary inside one test class is worse than consistency. Do not add a captor where asserting the returned graph suffices.
Framework transport boundary: MockMvc, the one sanctioned mock (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy). Drives real binding, validation, and view selection.

Persistence boundary for the replace-not-append criterion: prove it with real I/O in ClinicServiceTests (@DataJpaTest, real database, no doubles), mirroring shouldUpdatePetName and shouldAddNewVisitForPet. A mocked-repository controller test can only show the in-memory graph; the criterion is about what is stored.

patterns.description: findPet: @ModelAttribute loader taking @PathVariable(name=..., required=false) and branching on null. loadPetWithVisit takes the same shape for visitId, since it is controller-wide and must serve both the booking URLs (no visitId) and the correction URLs.

Owner.getPet(Integer): traversal from the aggregate root to a child by identity. Add Pet.getVisit(Integer) as its mirror and resolve the visit through it. Traversal belongs in the model, not in the controller (architecture-principles Pattern Catalog, Web controller row: binds, delegates, selects the response).

updatePetDetails: the change is written through the aggregate root by saving the Owner. The correction does the same. Note the simplification available here: because the bound visit IS the instance already inside pet.getVisits(), binding mutates the aggregate member in place and owners.save(owner) cascades an UPDATE. No copy-onto-existing step is needed, and none should be added.

The non-future-date rejection with error code typeMismatch.visitDate on field date. Extract it into one private helper called by both handlers. Do not paste a second copy into the correction handler: architecture-principles Pattern Catalog states a new rule added to a controller is a fresh violation not covered by the existing deviation. One rule with two callers leaves the recorded deviation the same size; two copies enlarge it.

risks.risk: Silent extra visit. loadPetWithVisit today unconditionally does new Visit() plus pet.addVisit(visit). If that side effect still runs on the correction path, owners.save(owner) cascade-inserts a blank second visit and the acceptance criterion 'the pet has no more visits than before' fails, while the happy-path redirect test still passes.
risks.mitigation: The correction branch returns the existing visit and never calls pet.addVisit. Keep the addVisit call inside the visitId == null branch only. The persistence-level proof lives in ClinicServiceTests (see integration_points).

risks.risk: A visitId that belongs to another pet or another owner is an insecure-direct-object-reference surface (security-principles Trust Boundaries, external input arrives; Realization row 'Trusting cross-request state').
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only by traversing owner -> pet -> visit, never by a global lookup; there is no VisitRepository, so the traversal is the only path. A visitId absent from that pet's visits is refused with IllegalArgumentException, the same refusal mechanism the loader already uses for a pet that is not the named owner's (PRD Visits edge case 1). This delivers PRD edge case 3.

risks.risk: New user-facing text breaks the i18n gates. src/test/java/.../system/I18nPropertiesSyncTest.java fails on any literal text in an HTML line, and fails on any key missing from one of the eleven bundles (REQ-LANG-002).
risks.mitigation: Change no user-facing text. The template is expected to need no change at all: the form carries no th:action so it posts to the current URL, and the heading and previous-visits guards already branch on visit['new']. The submit button keeps reading #{addVisit} on the correction form; no requirement states the label, and a new key would cost eleven translations this slice was not asked for. This is a decision, not an oversight.

risks.risk: A hard-coded confirmation flash message would be a fresh REQ-LANG-002 violation. The booking path's 'Your visit has been booked' is a hard-coded Java literal that the i18n test does not scan, so copying the pattern looks safe.
risks.mitigation: Add no flash message on the correction path. REQ-VIS-003 requires only that the owner's record is shown, so redirect:/owners/{ownerId} with no flash attribute is the narrowest reading. If a later requirement asks for a confirmation, it arrives with a message key in every bundle.

risks.risk: Mass assignment through the new binding (security-principles Realization row 'Mass assignment').
risks.mitigation: The existing controller-wide @InitBinder setAllowedFields disallows id and *.id and already covers the new mappings. Do not narrow it, and do not add a mapping-scoped binder without the same disallow list. The visit identity therefore comes from the path variable only, never from the form.

risks.risk: Replacing the bound validator would silently drop the description-required rule. PetController does dataBinder.setValidator(new PetValidator()), which replaces bean validation, which is why PetValidator re-checks fields the entity already annotates.
risks.mitigation: Introduce no VisitValidator in this slice. Visit's @NotBlank description must keep firing through the default bean-validation path so the blank-description refusal names the field. The Form validator pattern remains the sanctioned home for the date rule if a later slice moves it out of the controller.

notes: Both PRD open questions taken at their narrowest reading, per the dispatch instruction; neither opens a consultation. (1) No visible entry point: ownerDetails.html gains no link and is not a target of this slice. (2) A past-dated visit: the future-date rule applies to the correction exactly as to a booking, with no unchanged-date exemption and no special case; PRD edge case 4 is the expected behavior, not a defect to work around. | Observed consequence, recorded so it is not mistaken for a defect: on the correction form visit['new'] is false, so the Previous Visits table renders the pet's visits including the one being corrected, and the heading reads 'Visit' rather than 'New Visit'. The template's th:if/th:each pair filters the not-yet-persisted visit on the booking form, which is how REQ-VIS-002 is delivered today; leave that guard alone. | Suggested handler flow for the correction POST: reject a non-future date through the shared helper, return the form view on binding errors, otherwise owners.save(owner) and redirect. The bound visit is already the pet's own instance, so a rejected submission leaves the in-memory graph dirty and nothing saved; the owner is re-fetched per request and spring.jpa.open-in-view is off, so nothing persists. | Pet.getVisits() is a LinkedHashSet and BaseEntity overrides neither equals nor hashCode, so mutating a member already in the set is safe. | No autofix audit findings: the log contains no design-doc-autofix records. | Coverage claims above rest on grep and direct file reads, the weaker basis; the IntelliJ oracle is not connected in this run.

author: review-planner
rationale: code-quality-reviewer: new production rule (visit correction) and its Pet/VisitController placement need a design-placement check; test-reviewer: new tests and a new rule's test placement need a look even though behavior is straightforward; security-reviewer: the new /visits/{visitId}/edit routes take user-supplied path variables and gate access via an ownership check (pet.getVisit throwing on mismatch), a trust-boundary path worth verifying; doc-reviewer: PRD, system-design, and two ADRs were rewritten to describe this exact behavior change, so their coherence with the code needs review; the change itself is contained to one module with a clean, well-tested slice, so overall risk is low despite the full roster.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: Pet.getVisit(Integer) mirrors Owner.getPet(Integer) exactly (traversal, null-not-found, javadoc shape, !isNew() guard) — consistent-with-codebase placement of the aggregate traversal in the model rather than the controller
VisitController.loadPetWithVisit's new visitId branch keeps pet.addVisit confined to the booking (visitId == null) path, avoiding the silent-extra-visit risk the design-block flagged

The non-future-date rule was extracted into one private rejectVisitDateNotInFuture helper shared by both POST handlers instead of being duplicated, keeping the existing controller-rule deviation the same size per architecture-principles' Pattern Catalog

Not-found handling for a mismatched visit reuses the existing IllegalArgumentException idiom and message shape already used for a mismatched pet, so the new refusal path reads as the established convention rather than a new one
No flash message and no template change on the correction path, correctly avoiding a fresh REQ-LANG-002 (i18n) violation as the design-block called for
New comments (Pet.java javadoc, VisitController's three added/modified comments) explain WHY — framework call ordering and in-place-mutation rationale — none restates what the code already says
checkFormatMain/Test and checkstyleMain pass clean; no TODO/FIXME/System.out/printStackTrace introduced
Change stays within the slice's acceptance criteria and the narrowed NG-5 boundary; no cancellation, deletion, or pet-reassignment capability was added

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain was not verified against the NVD in this review: build.gradle configures no OWASP dependency-check plugin and the reviewer has no network access, so no CVE matching ran. The change adds no dependency, so the resolved set is unchanged from the last verified state -- but treat the check as 'not run', and have CI or a human close it against the pinned Spring Boot 4.1.0 line.

processUpdateVisitForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner, so a POST to the correction URL also data-binds request parameters onto the loaded owner (firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone) and persists them via owners.save(owner), with no @Valid on owner and its BindingResult never inspected. This exactly mirrors the pre-existing processNewVisitForm, and with no authentication in the demonstration baseline it grants no privilege a caller lacks at /owners/{id}/edit, so it is not a finding. It does add a second URL from which owner fields are writable without bean validation; if the pattern is ever revisited, fix both handlers together rather than only the new one.

On a rejected correction, binding has already mutated the managed Visit instance in place before rejectVisitDateNotInFuture runs. No flush follows (Spring's open-session-in-view sets MANUAL flush outside a transaction, and the error path only reads), and PetController's edit path has the same shape, so nothing persists today. Worth remembering as a constraint if a future change introduces a transaction or an explicit flush into the error path.
approved_aspects: Aggregate-scoped resolution prevents IDOR: loadPetWithVisit re-resolves owner -> pet -> visit on every request (owners.findById, owner.getPet(petId), pet.getVisit(visitId)) and throws when the chain does not hold, so a correction naming an owner, pet, and visit that do not belong together is refused rather than applied. Satisfies the security brief's 'Trusting cross-request state' row.

Mass assignment control intact: the class-level @InitBinder in VisitController keeps setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id"), which covers the newly bound 'visit' and 'owner' model attributes on both new endpoints. Identifier binding stays impossible, matching OwnerController and PetController.

Validation is not weakened on the correction path: the extracted rejectVisitDateNotInFuture is byte-identical to the rule it replaces on the booking path and is applied to both handlers, and @Valid Visit keeps @NotBlank on description. No divergence between the two write paths.

Correction mutates the pet's own Visit instance rather than adding one, so no duplicate row and no id juggling; Pet.getVisit skips unpersisted visits and uses Objects.equals, so a null or unmatched id yields null rather than a false match.

No new exception message carries sensitive data: the added IllegalArgumentException names only caller-supplied ids, the same shape as the pre-existing owner/pet messages, so the error page's known detail-leak defect is not widened.

Output escaping unchanged: createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is not touched, renders every value through th:text, and the repository-wide sweep found no th:utext and no Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__) anywhere in templates.

Diff sweep for injection, deserialization, shell execution, file I/O, system /tmp, java.util.Random, System.out/err and hardcoded credentials over all 358 added lines returned no hits. No build.gradle change, so no new dependency and no widened supply-chain surface.
Controller state stays request-scoped: the singleton holds only the final OwnerRepository, and the new handler introduces no shared mutable field.

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction of a booked visit

blast_radius.note: Contained: 59 production lines across two files in the single owner package (Pet.getVisit plus two new VisitController handlers), no sensitive paths, no dependency or config change; the remaining files are tests and docs.

semantic_surprise.note: No hidden logic inversion — the future-date rule is extracted byte-identical and the edit path returns the pet's own Visit without calling addVisit — but the new POST binds @ModelAttribute Owner with no @Valid and then saves it, so a correction request carrying firstName/address/telephone rewrites the owner; that mirrors processNewVisitForm exactly, yet it is a second URL doing more than 'correct a visit' implies.

test_adequacy.note: Tests assert real outcomes, not the implementation: the controller test checks the pet's own Visit instance was mutated and the visit count unchanged, ClinicServiceTests proves update-not-insert with a real flush/clear round trip, and the boundary (today, yesterday, blank description) is covered parameterized.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four approved with empty findings, but two parked reservations in recommendations: the security reviewer records supply-chain/CVE matching as not run (no network, no dependency-check plugin) and flags the owner-binding reach on the new URL, and the test reviewer notes the id-identity test passes regardless of whether the POST succeeded.

scope_deviation.note: Stayed on its triage: one build retry, zero consultations, zero design revisions, and the diff matches REQ-VIS-003 plus the NG-5 narrowing the intake decision authorized — no cancellation, deletion, or UI link crept in.

rationale: Reviewers found nothing and the persistence path is well proven. Read two things before merging: the new POST handler's unvalidated @ModelAttribute Owner binding, which lets a correction request rewrite owner fields, and the security reviewer's unrun supply-chain check.
